stop_condition: Each of the four round-2 HIGH findings is shown FIXED or NOT FIXED by independent re-measurement rather than by reading the correction; every claim the corrections introduce is itself checked for falsity, with the read-only proposition swept across the whole repo (not just the files the brief names) and every negative grep backed by a positive control on the same input; the five CI facts the test.yml block cites are verified against run 36971074875 itself; the C9 inference-as-observation question is answered for each new sentence; the cheap checks pass at their stated counts; and the working tree is shown byte-identical before and after.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh:396-397 (--help body, operator-facing) and .claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md:62-64 (the MANIFESTED skill) — both lines ARE in this diff
findings.evidence: NEW TEXT, NEW FALSE CLAIM. Both corrected surfaces close the dolt paragraph with a causal attribution: --help :396-397 reads 'the delta is 0 only when stats already exists, which is why the original 6,936-file run reported three files and nothing else'; the skill :62-64 reads 'which is why the original 6,936-file measurement saw nothing'. GIT ARCHAEOLOGY FALSIFIES IT. `git log --oneline --reverse -S'6,936' -- .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh` returns exactly ONE commit, ff38ee8 (2026-07-28 22:54 +0400) — the sentence has never been re-measured since. `git log --oneline --reverse -S'schema_migrations' -- <same file>` returns 33e45fa (2026-08-16 14:41 +0700) as the first. AT ff38ee8 THE DOCTOR CONTAINED NO DOLT CALL AT ALL: `git show ff38ee8:.claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh | grep -c -i 'dolt'` -> 0, and `| grep -c 'schema_migrations'` -> 0; POSITIVE CONTROL on the identical pipeline against the identical input, `| grep -c 'check_beads'` -> 3, so an empty result would have been meaningful. The SELECT landed 19 days AFTER the measurement. The same applies to the companion citation: `10,358` also enters at ff38ee8 only. So the 6,936-file run could not have executed the SELECT, and the reason it reported three files is that the code which creates `.dolt/stats` did not yet exist — not that the target's store already carried stats. The store state of that 2026-07-28 target is unrecorded and is not what produced the result.
findings.description: A correction that is itself false, which is the pattern this round exists to catch, and false in the UNSAFE direction for the third time in this release. The sentence tells a reader the original measurement DID exercise the SELECT and found it benign because stats pre-existed — i.e. that the 6,936-file figure remains valid evidence about what the CURRENT code touches, merely conditioned on one variable. It is not: it is evidence about a code path that did not contain a dolt call. A reader (or a future QA re-deriving the side-effect inventory) who trusts it will treat a pre-dolt measurement as current and will not re-run it. One of the two surfaces is `.claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md`, manifest row 12 of manifests/v5.0.0.sha256, so this ships. Note what is NOT wrong: the author's account of their OWN recent delta-0 runs, at workflow-doctor.sh:1450-1452 ('two delta-0 runs against samples that already carried stats'), makes no 6,936 claim and is consistent with everything I measured — the defect is confined to the attribution about the 2026-07-28 measurement, which appears only in --help and the skill.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh:61-62 (file header) and :1364-1366 (the beads check's OWN header) — both UNMODIFIED by this diff
findings.evidence: DIRECT ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S FIX-2 QUESTION: YES, surfaces still assert it, and the belief that 'the others concern --skip beads' is wrong for both. The diff touches four hunks only (`git diff -U0` @@ markers: 149, 154-170, 373-382, 1415-1416), so neither line moved. (1) :61-62 — 'MEASURED, not assumed. On an isolated 6,936-file target: a full run changed exactly those three .beads/* files and nothing else'. This is textually the SAME sentence as the --help one the author DID correct ('Measured on a 6,936-file target: a full run changed exactly those three and nothing else'); the `--skip beads` clause is the NEXT clause, not this one. (2) :1364-1366 — 'This is the only file change a full run makes anywhere in the target (QA verified against an isolated 10,358-file tree)'. This is the strongest of the four: no measurement qualifier, present tense, universally quantified ('anywhere in the target'), and it is FALSE by the file's own new text 30 lines later. Worse, the new comment CITES it as authority twice — :1441 'because this check's header tells an operator what a run touches' and :1467 'see this check's header'. Repo-wide sweep with positive control: `grep -rnIE '(exactly those three|only file change|ONLY things a full run|6,936|10,358)' --include='*.sh' --include='*.md' --include='*.yml' --include='Makefile'` returns these two plus the two corrected ones and nothing else outside e2e fixtures; POSITIVE CONTROL, same invocation shape, `grep -rcIE 'DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_VALIDATED'` over the same roots returns README.md:1, CHANGELOG.md:1, workflow-doctor.sh:16, workflow-doctor.test.sh:8, test.yml:5. CHECKED AND GENUINELY CLEAN (not the same proposition): Makefile:471-476, docs/HOOKS.md:3050 and docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:822 all describe `beads` as the exception and say only that `--skip beads` provably touches nothing — true, and I MEASURED the `--skip beads` half rather than inheriting it (see R3-F6). COMPOUNDING: both surviving citations (6,936 and 10,358) are from ff38ee8, 19 days before the dolt SELECT existed — see R3-F1 — so each rests on a measurement that provably could not have exercised the effect it is being read as having excluded.
findings.description: R2-F3 is NOT discharged. The correction was again scoped to sentences rather than to the proposition: two of the four restatements were fixed, two were left, and the two left are in the very file being edited — one of them the header of the very function being edited, which the new comment then points the reader at. The practical failure mode is exact: an operator or agent who follows :1467's 'see this check's header' lands on :1364-1366 and reads 'This is the only file change a full run makes anywhere in the target', which the 70 lines above it have just withdrawn. Nothing mechanical will catch this — workflow-doctor.test.sh Section 5c (:1036-1050) asserts only that each of the three surfaces contains the literal 'EXCEPT `beads`' and the token 'WAL'; it does not pin the exclusivity sentence, so correcting it breaks nothing and leaving it fails nothing (228/228 assertions pass at this tree with the inconsistency present).

findings.evidence: The new comment states: 'TWO OTHER SURFACES CARRIED THE SAME ERROR and were corrected in the same pass, because a side-effect inventory an operator relies on is useless if only one copy of it is right: this file's own --help text (which said a full run changes exactly three files and nothing else) and .claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md, the manifested skill, which said the same.' Its description of what those two said is ACCURATE (verified against `git show HEAD:` for both). What is false is the COUNT and the completeness it asserts: at least two more surfaces carried the same error and were not corrected (:61-62 and :1364-1366 — see R3-F2 for the sweep and its positive control). So 'TWO OTHER SURFACES CARRIED THE SAME ERROR' is a count of surfaces CORRECTED, presented as a count of surfaces AFFECTED, and the clause that follows it ('a side-effect inventory ... is useless if only one copy of it is right') asserts the sweep's rationale as satisfied when it is not.
findings.description: This is structurally the same defect round 2 recorded as R2-F3's sharpest part — the sentence that declared the skill 'unaffected' — relocated rather than removed. The author replaced a false positive non-impact claim about another file with a false completeness claim about the sweep, and in both cases the sentence is a POSITIVE assertion about files the author did not check at the moment of writing it. It matters more than an ordinary miscount because of where it sits: it is the one place a future reader is told the inventory is now internally consistent, so it is precisely the sentence that stops the next reader from re-running the sweep. Filed separately from R3-F2 because they are independently actionable: R3-F2 is two sentences to fix, R3-F3 is this sentence being true only after they are.

findings.evidence: ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S C9 QUESTION: the sentence is NEITHER marked as inference NOR entailed, though it is strongly supported and I cannot show it false. The text reads, flat present tense: 'The binary at the pinned path is replaced in place at some point during the suite. What performs the replacement is NOT established and is deliberately not guessed at here.' WHAT I ACTUALLY OBSERVED in run 36971074875's l1-unit job: `bd version` -> 1.1.2 (20e493e56) at 05:54:59 in the Install step and again at 05:55:08 in Verify dependencies; `/usr/local/bin/bd --version` -> 1.3.1 (c1c4b642a) at 06:38:53 in the harness dump; one bd on PATH at that later moment ('bd is /usr/local/bin/bd', a single [1] entry); and exactly one beads download URL in the whole job (`grep -oE 'https://[^ "]*(beads|steveyegge)[^ "]*'` -> one hit, v1.1.2; POSITIVE CONTROL, same grep widened to `releases/download`, finds node, dolt and beads, so an empty result would have been meaningful). TWO LINKS ARE MISSING FROM THE CHAIN, and the text discloses neither. First, the two EARLY readings are PATH-RESOLVED `bd version` (test.yml:453 and the Verify-dependencies step), not absolute-path reads, and no `type -a` was dumped at those moments — so 'the binary AT THE PINNED PATH was 1.1.2 at 05:54:59' is itself inferred from the tarball having just been extracted there. Second, 'replaced in place' names a FILE-level mechanism; what is entailed by three version strings is only that the name resolved to different versions at different times. The sentence immediately after, by marking only the AGENT as unestablished, implicitly certifies the replacement itself as observed — drawing the evidential line one step further forward than the evidence reaches.
findings.description: Rubric C9 (.claude/rubrics/default.md v3), inference in the voice of an observation. Recorded at MEDIUM, explicitly NOT as a v5.0.0 blocker under the stated stop rule: I cannot show the claim false, and the surrounding file supplies strong independent prior for it (workflow-doctor.sh:122, :215, :222 all document bd self-upgrading in place on a dev host). The contrast with the author's own adjacent work is what makes this worth filing rather than waiving: in the README paragraph and the DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_VALIDATED entry the same material is handled correctly throughout — 'would have observed', 'is consistent with never having measured the floor at all', 'what is NOT established' — so the C9 discipline is being applied everywhere except this one sentence. v5.0.1 follow-up; the cheapest honest repair is to say what was read (three version strings at one path) and let the replacement be the stated inference it is.

findings.description: Downgraded from r2's HIGH to MEDIUM deliberately: the sentence r2 proved false is fixed, the retained entry carries an explicit, honest and sufficient justification at :172-174, and what remains is a prescription the set does not follow rather than an assertion that is false. The residual is still worth closing because the three restatements are the places a future maintainer reads when deciding whether to add a pair, and one of them is text an operator sees at the exact moment the check fails. Under the stated stop rule this is a v5.0.1 follow-up, not a v5.0.0 blocker.

findings.location: Verification record for FIX 1 and FIX 4 — what reproduced, and how
findings.evidence: FIX 1 IS CORRECT, re-derived on FOUR store shapes, not two. Host: bd 1.3.0 (f45b249ce), dolt 2.3.0 — the version the comment names. Isolated HOME/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/DOLT_ROOT_PATH under the session scratchpad; instrument `find <store> -mindepth 1 | sort` before/after, with a POSITIVE CONTROL run first on every arm (touched a probe; the diff printed exactly that path; probe removed and the pre-snapshot retaken). Running EXACTLY workflow-doctor.sh:1521-1522, `( cd <store> && dolt sql -r csv -q "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version),0) FROM schema_migrations" )`: EMPTY store, db named beads -> 11 -> 22, 11 added, 0 removed; POPULATED (5 issues), db named beads -> 11 added; POPULATED (2 issues), DEFAULT db name -> 11 added; EMPTY, DEFAULT db name -> 11 added. Every arm re-run with stats present -> 0 added, 0 removed. So 'contents are irrelevant', 'the only condition that matters is whether stats already exists' and 'when it does the delta is 0' are all correct, and so are the count (11) and the shape ('a nested .dolt with its own noms/, manifest and LOCK'). The gitignore sub-claim holds generally, not just here: `bd init` itself writes .beads/.gitignore with `embeddeddolt/`, and `git check-ignore -v` confirms in a FRESH fixture as well as in this repo. The re-asserted `--skip beads` half was MEASURED rather than inherited: `beads_ledger` is the other check that touches the real target, and its `bd export -o <mktemp>` leaves the whole .beads/ byte-identical (20 files hashed, 0 content diff) and creates no stats; `bd list` and `bd --version` likewise 0. ONE PRECISION NIT, not a finding: the 11 added paths are `.dolt/stats` itself plus 10 beneath it, so '11 paths under <store>/.dolt/stats/' (--help :394, skill :60-61) is 10 strictly under; the comment's own phrasing at :1444 ('11 paths, a nested .dolt with its own noms/, manifest and LOCK') has no such scoping and is exactly right. FIX 4: ALL FIVE CITED FACTS VERIFIED against run 36971074875 itself, not against the text. headSha=ed9ea91e6496ce13a5c080ad3cbbb2dc14ba7e66 (this HEAD), run conclusion=failure. (a) job 'L1 — bash unit tests' = FAILURE, with two 'FAIL: META-TEST 8a control: ...' lines. (b) 'installed bd 1.3.1 / store schema v66' present (2 occurrences). (c) the dump reads 'every bd on PATH, in resolution order: bd is /usr/local/bin/bd' with a single '[1] /usr/local/bin/bd -> bd version 1.3.1 (c1c4b642a)'. (d) exactly one beads download URL job-wide. (e) job 'L1 — workflow-doctor (bd max end)' = SUCCESS, disclosing '[8a] measured: bd-version-vs-schema pin OK: 1.3.0:66 is in the validated set: 1.1.2:53 1.3.0:66. Measured binary: /tmp/workflow-doctor.ev8AeS/bin/bd -> /usr/local/bin/bd'. Every log search carried a positive control on the same file ('Install bd' 33, '1.1.2' 6, 'META-TEST 8' 22 vs a known-absent sentinel at 0). TWO FACTS THE SHIPPED TEXT ASSERTS AND I STRENGTHENED RATHER THAN WEAKENED. The cited release time is exact: `gh release view v1.3.1 --repo steveyegge/beads` -> publishedAt 2026-09-30T23:37:36Z. And 'has not [passed] since' holds across the whole window, checked run by run rather than assumed: all five l1-unit jobs executed after that timestamp (110243629074, 110256370089, 110285108534, 110417577862, 110724973674) FAIL the 8a control, while the last l1-unit job before it, 109105524858 at 2026-09-28T19:48, PASSES both 8a control assertions — a clean before/after boundary that the shipped counterfactual ('would have observed 1.3.0:66 ... and passed') predicts. FINALLY, the one claim r2 left inherited is now re-derived: I downloaded beads_1.1.2_darwin_arm64.tar.gz, verified it against the release checksums.txt (9b0137a83a2afd343e2abd2a506be72ea032721000f76669c2cf81729e78501d, exact match), confirmed it is the same release commit CI installs (20e493e56), and ran its own `bd init` in two isolated fixtures: the doctor's exact query returns 53 on both (empty and 1-issue), against 66 for bd 1.3.0. So ':158-160 the pair itself is right' is now measured, not cited.

findings.location: Housekeeping and instrument notes for whoever approves
findings.evidence: CHEAP CHECKS, all green at this tree. `bash .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh` -> rc 0, 228 assertions (matching r2 and ed9ea91's stated count). `make lint` -> rc 0. `bash .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh generate . | diff - manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> IDENTICAL, 140 rows, and BOTH changed rows equal their files' live sha256 exactly (.claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md 198508e4e3bab8b346e499143387e433e1ae22d7858162aa6728884a2412e151; .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh 923dfcd59f12917d66ae97d1ac27d0d296b82dd37c86ef542711bf56bd6422bc). .github/workflows/test.yml parses as YAML (7 jobs enumerated) and the parser was shown to REJECT deliberately broken input, so the pass is not vacuous; test.yml is still unmanifested (0 rows). Two consumer specs also run clean: approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh 238/0, workflow-manifest.test.sh 230/0. IMPACT PASS. The persisted report at .claude/.qa-tracking/impact-report-claude-workflow-plugin-ishe.json still carries change_set_hash 50d59bb7... from the r1 cycle; the live set now hashes to 8299709500c73813cd773d06d2dc04850b0ca9c33d0cedba998b44c68bd8da18 across 8 tracked paths (the five modified files, plus workflow-doctor.test.sh which `git status` shows UNMODIFIED, plus the r1 and r2 review artifacts). `qa-gate.sh approve` will refuse until `impact-report.sh claude-workflow-plugin-ishe` is re-run. My own pass: the workflow-doctor.sh edit changes NO executable line — the only non-comment changed lines are the 14 inside usage()'s quoted heredoc (`<<'USAGE'` at :295, terminator at :442), so --help display text, with a positive control showing the same filter returns 15 changed lines for README.md; code-graph was live (not degraded) and `impact_of` on the file reports 0 file-level dependents and 65 name-matched nodes that are generic shell helper-name collisions, consistent with r2. GIT STATUS. Byte-identical before and after the entire review, verified in a clean shell: the five modified files and the r1/r2 artifacts, nothing else. No mirror was built and nothing was symlinked. ONE INSTRUMENT FALSE ALARM, recorded because the brief asks for affirmative evidence: mid-review a `git status` run from inside my measurement shell reported an EXTRA `?? .claude/settings.local.json`. It is not a change — the file is dated 2026-06-12 and is ignored via /Users/edk0/.config/git/ignore:1 (`**/.claude/settings.local.json`). The cause is my own fixture environment: `core.excludesFile` is unset, so git resolves the global ignore through $HOME/.config/git/ignore, and that shell had HOME pointed at an isolated fixture home. Reproduced deliberately both ways — with the real HOME the path matches 0 times, with the foreign HOME 1 time, while `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` alone does NOT reproduce it, so HOME is the variable and not GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL.
findings.description: Housekeeping for whoever approves, plus one methodological note. The stale impact report is a mechanical refusal waiting to happen, fixed by one command. The instrument false alarm is recorded in full because an isolated-HOME measurement silently disabling a repo's global gitignore is exactly the shape that would make a future reviewer report tree contamination that never happened — and this round's own brief was written because instruments lied in both prior rounds. Also worth the next editor's attention: nothing in the suite pins ANY of the corrected text. Section 5c of workflow-doctor.test.sh (:1036-1050) asserts only the literal 'EXCEPT `beads`' and 'WAL' in each surface, and the behavioural `--skip beads` test at :1092-1116 fingerprints only beads.db/-wal/-shm/issues.jsonl over a fixture with no real Dolt store, so it could not observe a .dolt/stats creation either way. The corrections and the inconsistencies R3-F2 leaves standing are equally invisible to the suite.
